text:
maggie: FYI got a report from a customer that our sample-payments app created duplicate charges after a burst of 429s. attaching logs below.

luke: ugh. reproducible locally?

maggie: yes, repro steps in thread: hit /create-payment concurrently (~8 reqs), then rotate token (simulated expired) causing SDK to refresh while some inflight requests hit 429 and retry. end result: two successful side-effectful calls.

sam: can you paste the relevant log snippet?

maggie: here's the critical part: 
```
2026-03-18T14:02:12Z INFO request id=abc123 status=429 retry=1
2026-03-18T14:02:12Z INFO auth refresh start token=expiring
2026-03-18T14:02:12Z INFO request id=def456 status=200
2026-03-18T14:02:12Z INFO request id=abc123 status=200 (after retry)
```
No idempotency keys were attached in the sample app.

devex-joe: two quick axes: (1) sample-app teach: always attach idempotency-key header for side effects; (2) SDK hardening: avoid replaying requests that raced with a token refresh + 429 sequence.

luke: SDK side is trickier because we need to keep streaming/simple retry behavior for stateless calls but protect side-effectful ones. proposals: token-refresh lock per-client, jittered wait before retry after 429 if a refresh just happened, and an optional replay-guard that tracks recent request fingerprints for N seconds.

sam: +1 on replay-guard, but footprint/time window needs tuning. we should also add a small random jitter on retries to avoid synchronized storms.

maggie: customer is on a PoC; want a short-term mitigation we can ship in sample-app docs and a medium-term SDK change.

devex-joe: short-term action items:
- update sample app README to show idempotency-key usage and small client-side debounce around create-payment endpoints (example code snippet)
- add note about token rotation causing duplicate side effects if idempotency not used

luke: medium-term SDK changes I can PR:
1) token refresh per-client mutex so only one inflight refresh occurs and others wait on the new token (opt-in flag to preserve current behavior)
2) attach a small replay-guard: in-memory LRU of recent request fingerprints (method+path+body hash + opt idempotency header) that will block replay for configurable window (default 10s)
3) jittered-backoff default for 429 with seeded rng to avoid sync.

sam: tests to add: e2e that simulates token-expiry mid-flight + 429s, assert no duplicate side effects when idempotency header missing and replay-guard enabled. also unit tests for mutex deadlock/fallback.

maggie: what about persistence for replay-guard in Dedicated/Private? in-memory won't survive process restarts.

luke: good question — make it pluggable: default in-memory for Hosted & dev, optional Redis-backed store for Dedicated/Private. document costs/consistency tradeoffs.

devex-joe: UX: crate a single tiny helper in SDKs: sdk.generateIdempotencyKey() and sample-app uses it by default. make the helper stable so users don't accidentally rotate keys too frequently.

maggie: owners?

luke: I'll pick up SDK work (eng-runtime + eng-platform collab).

sam: I'll add tests and help validate e2e scenarios.

devex-joe: I'll update sample-app + docs and add a short migration note for customers.

maggie: priority? customer is in PoC but it's potential money risk. mark P1 for sample app docs + quick README fix, P2 for SDK changes (but short timeline).

infra-bot: deploy-checklist created: #DC-472 refresh-debounce-replay-guard (assignee: luke) :white_check_mark:

luke: quick implementation detail question: for fingerprinting, do we include auth token id? that'd make replay-guard useless across token rotations. so do not include token. include content-type + body hash.

sam: agreed. and when idempotency header present, skip the fingerprint dedupe and defer to server-side semantics.

maggie: thanks all — i'll ping the customer with interim guidance: use idempotency keys and avoid simultaneous retries during token rotation. i'll follow up with a small note and the PR links. :thumbsup:

devex-joe: linking PRs as they land would be great. also add a short note in changelog about the opt-in mutex flag so customers know behavior change.

luke: will post draft PR by EOD tomorrow.

sam: will add e2e by Wed.

maggie: closing loop: followups in #devex tomorrow standup. thanks everyone.
